c01.display: Welcome back to NLP, Simply Explained. This is unit 3, lesson 2: dependency parsing.
c01.spoken: Welcome back to N L P, Simply Explained. This is unit 3, lesson 2: dependency parsing.

c02.display: Last time we drew sentences as trees of phrases. Today we draw them a different way: as links between words.
c02.spoken: Last time we drew sentences as trees of phrases. Today we draw them a different way: as links between words.

c03.display: Here's the idea. In a dependency tree, every word hangs off exactly one other word, and the main verb usually sits at the very top.
c03.spoken: Here's the idea. In a dependency tree, every word hangs off exactly one other word, and the main verb usually sits at the very top.

c04.display: A dependency is a link from a head word to a word that depends on it, with a label saying how they're related.
c04.spoken: A dependency is a link from a head word to a word that depends on it, with a label saying how they're related.

c05.display: In "Priya ate pizza", the word "pizza" depends on "ate". It's the object: the thing that was eaten.
c05.spoken: In "Priya ate pizza", the word "pizza" depends on "ate". It's the object: the thing that was eaten.

c06.display: Think of a family tree. Every word has exactly one parent, except the root at the top, which has none.
c06.spoken: Think of a family tree. Every word has exactly one parent, except the root at the top, which has none.

c07.display: Let's parse "Priya ate cold pizza". The labels in brackets are the short names used by Universal Dependencies, a standard used for over a hundred languages.
c07.spoken: Let's parse "Priya ate cold pizza". The labels in brackets are the short names used by Universal Dependencies, a standard used for over a hundred languages.

c08.display: Priya depends on ate. She's the subject: the one doing the eating.
c08.spoken: Priya depends on ate. She's the subject: the one doing the eating.

c09.display: Ate depends on nothing. It's the root of the whole sentence.
c09.spoken: Ate depends on nothing. It's the root of the whole sentence.

c10.display: Cold depends on pizza, because it describes the pizza.
c10.spoken: Cold depends on pizza, because it describes the pizza.

c11.display: And pizza depends on ate: it's the object, the thing that was eaten.
c11.spoken: And pizza depends on ate: it's the object, the thing that was eaten.

c12.display: How does this compare with last lesson's trees?
c12.spoken: How does this compare with last lesson's trees?

c13.display: A constituency tree nests phrases inside phrases, with labels like noun phrase and verb phrase. It shows the grammatical structure.
c13.spoken: A constituency tree nests phrases inside phrases, with labels like noun phrase and verb phrase. It shows the grammatical structure.

c14.display: A dependency tree links words directly, with labels like subject and object. It shows who did what to whom. They're two views of the same sentence.
c14.spoken: A dependency tree links words directly, with labels like subject and object. It shows who did what to whom. They're two views of the same sentence.

c15.display: This makes dependency trees very handy for reading off meaning. Start at the top.
c15.spoken: This makes dependency trees very handy for reading off meaning. Start at the top.

c16.display: The root tells you what happened: ate.
c16.spoken: The root tells you what happened: ate.

c17.display: The subject tells you who did it: Priya.
c17.spoken: The subject tells you who did it: Priya.

c18.display: The object tells you what it was done to: pizza.
c18.spoken: The object tells you what it was done to: pizza.

c19.display: And modifiers add extra detail: the pizza was cold.
c19.spoken: And modifiers add extra detail: the pizza was cold.

c20.display: One more idea from your syllabus: projectivity. A dependency tree is projective if you can draw all its links as arcs above the sentence, without any of them crossing.
c20.spoken: One more idea from your syllabus: projectivity. A dependency tree is projective if you can draw all its links as arcs above the sentence, without any of them crossing.

c21.display: Most English sentences are projective. Some sentences, and languages with freer word order, like Czech or Dutch, have links that cross. Those are called non-projective, and some parsers can't build them.
c21.spoken: Most English sentences are projective. Some sentences, and languages with freer word order, like Czech or Dutch, have links that cross. Those are called non-projective, and some parsers can't build them.

c22.display: Picture beads on a necklace, with strings tied between some of them. If none of the strings cross, the tree is projective.
c22.spoken: Picture beads on a necklace, with strings tied between some of them. If none of the strings cross, the tree is projective.

c23.display: Dependency parsing has become the most widely used kind. Three reasons.
c23.spoken: Dependency parsing has become the most widely used kind. Three reasons.

c24.display: It works well across many languages, including ones with free word order.
c24.spoken: It works well across many languages, including ones with free word order.

c25.display: It directly shows relations, which are easy to turn into facts: Priya, ate, pizza.
c25.spoken: It directly shows relations, which are easy to turn into facts: Priya, ate, pizza.

c26.display: And fast parsers can build the tree step by step, one move at a time. That's next lesson.
c26.spoken: And fast parsers can build the tree step by step, one move at a time. That's next lesson.

c27.display: Quick quiz. In "Priya ate cold pizza", which word does "cold" depend on?
c27.spoken: Quick quiz. In "Priya ate cold pizza", which word does "cold" depend on?

c29.display: It's pizza. Cold describes the pizza, so pizza is its head.
c29.spoken: It's pizza. Cold describes the pizza, so pizza is its head.

c30.display: Let's recap. In a dependency tree, every word hangs off one head word.
c30.spoken: Let's recap. In a dependency tree, every word hangs off one head word.

c31.display: The main verb is usually the root at the top.
c31.spoken: The main verb is usually the root at the top.

c32.display: Each link has a label, like subject or object, saying how the words relate.
c32.spoken: Each link has a label, like subject or object, saying how the words relate.

c33.display: And a tree is projective if its links can be drawn without crossing.
c33.spoken: And a tree is projective if its links can be drawn without crossing.

c34.display: Next lesson: Transition Parsing. How can a parser build a tree one move at a time?
c34.spoken: Next lesson: Transition Parsing. How can a parser build a tree one move at a time?
